frontier.hypothesis: A moved_once carrier that emits zero net bytes would close the function on the shipped chassis with ordinary C, because the carrier arrangement already reproduces the target's movable table exactly and only costs +7 instructions.
frontier.mechanism: With the carrier between the base-address computation and the first division, the requirement is only 2*insn_count > 116 and insn_count <= 122 (insn_count >= 59, i.e. +3 RTL insns over the baseline 56) - fifteen times cheaper than the +64 the s6 balanced-biv form needed. The blocker is purely that moved_once[] is written only at loop.c:1912, so the carrier must be a real loop and a real loop emits a backward branch.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate loop shapes whose control flow is fully removed AFTER loop_optimize: (a) an inner loop whose biv is eliminated by strength_reduce and whose remaining compare is folded by cse2/jump2 (check the .jump2 and .cse2 dumps, not the .loop dump); (b) a do{...}while(0) whose body begins with a CODE_LABEL that survives jump_optimize, which would defeat the 'is phony' rejection at loop.c:566-576 that killed rejected/dowhile0-inner-loop-is-phony.c - note do-while(0) is a SANCTIONED family (.claude/rules/do-while-zero-exception.md) so a byte-free instance would be admissible with a FAKE annotation. Measure byte cost with sandbox, and confirm 'halved since already moved' appears in the .loop dump.

frontier.hypothesis: An insn_count-inflation attack must land in the 3-wide window [120,122] (no carrier) or make 2*insn_count land in (116,122] (with a carrier); a form that overshoots breaks the match from the other side by declining the base-address hoist.
frontier.mechanism: The base address is movable slot 1 at threshold 122 and the /1800 magic is slot 2 at threshold 119; both have lifetime 1 and savings 1, so they can only be separated by an insn_count strictly between them. Measured directly: at effective insn_count 126 both printed 'not desirable' and the preheader lost its lui/addiu $a2 pair.
frontier.next_probe: Any future free-insn_count candidate must be swept across k and the .loop dump checked for the four-line pattern 'base moved / magic not desirable / 0x88888889 moved', not just for a lower sandbox score. Re-check whether s6's balanced-biv sweep has any k in [120,122] other than 121 - the window's width bounds how much slack a natural carrier is allowed.

frontier.hypothesis: A second loop LATER in the function that assigns an invariant to the same user variable our loop assigns would set moved_once without nesting, and might reuse control flow the function already has.
frontier.mechanism: loop_optimize scans loops in reverse order, so a sibling loop appearing after ours is scanned first; if it hoists a pseudo that our loop also sets exactly once, moved_once[regno] is already set when our loop is scanned. Unlike the nested case the carrier's set would not need to sit inside our loop's preheader.
frontier.next_probe: Confirm with a diagnostic that a later sibling loop assigning the same C local an invariant really produces ONE pseudo (not two) - RTL may split the variable. If it does, the question becomes whether the function's post-loop tail (func_8001CD68 through gpu_DisableDisplay, 8003C844..8003C89C, 23 instructions) can host a zero-byte loop; the shipped tail is straight-line, so the honest answer is probably no, but the pseudo-identity question is cheap to settle and it is the only non-nested route to moved_once.
